_comment: Run-local scoring weights for the Secret Loyalties Hackathon (2026-07-24 to 2026-07-26). NOT written to config/teams.yaml: TeamType is a closed Literal in src/saim/config/schemas.py and adding a 'hackathon' value would require a schema + test change the coordinator did not authorise. These weights are embedded directly into the scoring/refine prompts for this run only.

rationale.narrow_scope: 5.0 — ~40h of focused team work from kickoff to a hard submission deadline. A self-contained first deliverable is the binding constraint; an idea without one cannot ship.
rationale.accessible_complexity: 3.5 — mostly first-time Apart participants, early-career, limited hands-on interpretability/RLHF/evals experience.
rationale.low_compute: 3.0 — RAISED from 0.0, which every team in teams.yaml uses. Justified because this event explicitly provides NO compute ('plan to use your own') and recommends Qwen 0.5B-1B on modest hardware. Compute cost is a real filter here, unlike in the standard SAIM setting where it was zeroed out.
rationale.theory_of_impact: 2.5 — still matters for judging, but partially pre-satisfied: the organisers vetted all five tracks as safety-relevant, so it discriminates less between ideas than usual.
rationale.counterfactual_value: 2.5 — kept high per the coordinator's standing priority for work valuable outside major labs. Slightly below the mentor_novice 3.0 because the entire secret-loyalties agenda is outside-lab and neglected by construction, compressing the range.
rationale.novelty: 2.5 — REVISED UP from an initial 2.0 after retrieving the actual judging rubric from the Guidelines tab. Dimension 1 (Impact Potential & Innovation) explicitly gates the top marks on novelty: 'For scores of 4-5: is this actually new to the field, or replicating recent work?' A 5 requires 'a genuinely novel approach, or opens a new research direction'; a 2 is 'generic or well-trodden approach. Incremental at best.' Separately, the FAQ states 'Undisclosed prior work can lead to disqualification', which makes novelty a submission-risk issue and not merely a scoring one. The initial 2.0 was set from the track descriptions alone ('Negative results count'), which understated how much judges weight novelty. The tension is real but resolvable: the rubric also awards 4 for work that 'identifies a neglected problem area', so a replication-with-a-twist that lands a surprising negative result on a neglected question can still score highly. 2.5 reflects that balance.

novelty_gate_policy: Calculated novelty runs on all proposals. 'already_solved' drops the idea EXCEPT where the hackathon explicitly solicits that class of work (replication, defense benchmark, negative result), in which case it is flagged and retained. Both counts reported. Note the judging rubric's disqualification risk for undisclosed prior work makes the calculated-novelty pass mandatory rather than optional for this run.
dual_use_constraint: Retrieved VERBATIM from the Guidelines tab (Framer RSC payload decode; the tab is JS-rendered and WebFetch alone reports it as unreachable, which is a tooling artifact). Two firm guardrails: (1) do not jailbreak models to generate harmful data (terrorism, assassination, serious harms) to build organisms — use organiser-provided organisms and benign datasets; (2) do not publicly post novel secret-loyalty installation methods before organiser review; submit privately first. Working poison data is an explicit info-hazard and must not be published. A 'Limitations and Dual-Use Considerations' appendix is a REQUIRED submission element. Apart's jury applies a four-level disclosure policy (Highest/High/Intermediate/Low) as part of judging. KEY ASYMMETRY: novel offensive recipes are publish-gated, not research-gated; defenses, detection, benchmarks and negative results are unconstrained. Every generated idea must be statable as a defensive lesson without shipping the recipe. Caveat: the sprint page was still being edited on 2026-07-15 (both 'ongoing' and 'concluded' template variants present, only 2 of N talks scheduled), so guardrail text could change before the event — re-check closer to 2026-07-24.

assets_confirmed.petri_repo: github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_petri (github.com/safety-research/petri now redirects here; transferred out of Anthropic to Meridian Labs + UK AISI Red Team). v3.0 has Python-API breaks vs 2.0 — prefer the CLI and pin the version. Ships a literal secret_loyalty_probe seed plus US/Russia/China/Xi censorship probes among 173 defaults. Inspect supports vllm/ and hf/ providers, so Petri can target the HuggingFace organisms directly. enable_prefill defaults to False and MUST be set true for the prefill audits Track 2 asks for; local targets support prefill even though frontier APIs do not.
assets_confirmed.petri_target_caveat: Qwen 0.5B-1B organisms are likely too weak to engage Petri's synthetic-tool and multi-turn machinery, making judge scores noise rather than evidence. The 7B/32B organisms are the credible Petri targets; 0.5-1B are for fine-tuning experiments only.

track_numbering_hazard: The live sprint page has 5 tracks; the Resources doc has 4 and is an older cut. Doc T2 (Attack Feasibility) = live T4; doc T3 = live T2 + T3; doc T4 (Threat Modelling) = live T5. 'Track 4' therefore means the ATTACK track on the live page but the THREAT-MODELLING track in the doc. All track references in this run use LIVE-PAGE numbering.
